title: Equivariant tensor sheafification and the identity tensor
statement: Fix R,P,H as in [def-sfb-condensed-tensor-induction-data]. For every TensorInductionPresheaf B, there exists TensorInductionSheafData B: a functor L, its natural comparison with ordinary module sheafification, the induced-action and map formulas, and the H-equivariant identity tensor morphism. No adjunction or extension property is asserted.

source.place: Agent-formulated induction argument below paragraph (3); Equivariant tensor sheafification and the identity tensor. External reference WANTED, as for the parent.

proof.text: Continuous maps into P form a sheaf of groups: descend compatible maps along finite coproduct covering surjections, which are quotient by compactness and the Hausdorff property. Empty covers are included.

Apply equivariant module sheafification to B and realize the sheaf and its action in the internal module category through the section-module equivalence. Unique extension of the maps gives functoriality, the comparison and the action/map formulas.

The identity tensor is linear and natural. The balanced relation identifies [h] tensor m with [1] tensor hm, so equivariance of the sheafification unit makes it H-equivariant. Full faithfulness of the section-module equivalence supplies the corresponding internal-module morphism.
